subject: VPC/on-prem capacity sensitivity & handoff — private GPU pool
messages:
From: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@stratoslabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private pool sizing request — Stratos pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking this on. We want to move forward with a private VPC deployment for our inference workloads and need a pragmatic capacity plan for the initial pilot (US-West). High level asks:

- Throughput sizing for a ~6 week pilot (forecasted QPS and peak bursts)
- Network & egress constraints for our on‑prem gateway topology
- Sizing sensitivity (what happens if 2x burst or 3x baseline)
- A short ops handoff checklist we can use to provision the environment and validate performance

Attached is our rough traffic trace and the model mix (stratos_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) plus a simple topology diagram.

Key constraints to note:
- We have two primary models: conversational medium (avg 512 tokens) and reranker (short calls ~32 tokens).
- Target 99th p99 latency: conversational <= 300ms, reranker <= 80ms.
- Expected sustained baseline: 18 QPS conversational, 30 QPS reranker. Peak bursts up to 8x for short windows (1–3 minutes).

Can your team sketch an initial sensitivity table and a recommended minimum GPU pool and network egress recommendation we can commit to for the pilot? Procurement timeline: we need final numbers by Oct 8 to lock in hardware ordering.

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering, Stratos Labs
ops@stratoslabs.com

1) Sensitivity table covering baseline, 2x and 4x sustained, and 8x microbursts (1–5 minutes).
2) Minimum GPU pool recommendation (type + count), warm‑pool sizing, and coldstart/cold cache mitigation notes.
3) Network egress profile and NIC/crossconnect guidance for the VPC gateway + recommended headroom.
4) Ops handoff checklist: validation queries, KV cache warmup steps, observability checks (token-level latency, tail percentiles), and a short playbook for graceful degradation.

If convenient, can you confirm those three items by EOD Oct 5? We'll draft the initial sensitivity workbook and include a simple runbook for ops handoff.

Following up — I pulled the traffic trace and started an initial back‑of‑envelope. Outlining key engineering assumptions here so we converge quickly:

Assumptions used (preliminary):
- Conversational model: GPU type A100‑40GB (fp16) baseline throughput estimate 60 tokens/s per GPU core under continuous batching; avg request costs ~512 tokens (input+output).
- Reranker: CPU+GPU hybrid, but assume each 8‑GPU shard can handle ~50 qps of 32‑token reranking calls with batching.
- KV/prefix caching: assume warm cache for 70% of conversational traffic during steady state (affects tokens generated).
- Concurrency: 1.8 concurrent inflight requests per QPS for conversation workload (due to generation time).
- Networking: plan for 25% headroom on egress at baseline, 50% for 2x sustained.

Preliminary sizing (very conservative):
- Baseline (18 conv + 30 rerank): 6x A100‑40GB GPUs dedicated (with multiplexing and batching) + 2x 40Gb NICs with 50% egress headroom. Warm pool 2 GPUs for quick absorption.
- 2x sustained: 12 GPUs.
- Microbursts (8x for 2 minutes): rely on warm pool + short autoscale burst to cloud/dedicated if available; otherwise would need 20 GPUs to absorb purely on‑prem.

I'll attach the quick sheet with the math (small workbook) and a short sensitivity matrix. Key open items for flow refinement: exact token percentiles, batchability of reranker, and any procurement hard limits on NIC or crossconnect speeds.

Attachment: jonas_privpool_math_v1.xlsx

Happy to walk through these numbers on the call — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — that framing helps. A few clarifications from our side:

- Conversational concurrency: clients are single‑model; we do not multiplex across model families. Typical inflight concurrency for conversation is closer to 2.2 due to occasional longer completions.
- Token distribution: p50=420, p90=920, p99=1600 (we underreported tail earlier).
- Reranker: can tolerate batching up to 50ms extra latency; so aggressive batching is OK during peak.
- Procurement limits: maximum NIC per host is 100Gb (we can provision 2x 100Gb for the gateway if recommended).
- Disaster/failover: we want a regional failover plan but for pilot we won't provision full second region — just a cold failover document.

Procurement note: If we can provide a final hardware recommendation (GPU count/type + NICs + minimum SSD IOps) by Oct 8, our procurement team will start vendor quotes on Oct 9. We're targeting a soft launch Oct 25.

I'll be on the Oct 6 call.

Alex

Subject: Re: Private pool sizing request — Stratos pilot

Alex / team — thanks for the fast clarifications. Summary of decisions and next actions (handoff friendly):

Decisions made
- Baseline commit for pilot: 8x A100‑40GB equivalent GPUs (accounts for p90 token tail and concurrency 2.2).
- Warm pool: reserve 3 GPUs for immediate burst absorption (warm cache strategy + prewarmed containers).
- NICs: provision 2x100Gb uplinks at the gateway with a target egress headroom of 50% at baseline.
- Reranker: place on a separate 4‑GPU shard with aggressive batching enabled; keep CPU fallback for very short requests.
- Autoscale policy: short autoscale window for microbursts (1–5 minutes) to a temporary cap of 20 GPUs; fallback to graceful degradation (priority queueing) if autoscale fails.

Operational acceptance criteria (what ops team must validate before soft launch)
- End‑to‑end p99 latency validation: conversational <= 300ms for p90 traffic and <= 600ms for p99 given tail; reranker p99 <= 80ms.
- KV cache warmup: >70% hit rate within 10 minutes of steady traffic following deployment.
- Observability: token‑level telemetry, tail latency dashboards, and alerting on NIC saturation at 80%.
- Failover doc: cold failover checklist to spin up remote pool and traffic cutover steps (owner: Laura).

Deliverables by Oct 8 (we'll send these as separate artifacts):
- Final capacity sheet with exact GPU math and NIC recommendations (Jonas).
- Ops handoff checklist + acceptance runbook (Soojin + Karthik).
- Procurement-ready spec (Laura) including SSD IOps and cabling notes.

Call to action: Laura — please start the procurement spec sheet and vendor contact list. Jonas/Karthik — finalize the sensitivity workbook and include cost/leadtimes notes. Alex — flag any hard constraints from procurement we should know now.

I'll attach the draft runbook and signal Jira ticket for the handoff.

Attachments: runbook_draft.md, JIRA-INFRA-4123

Thanks — Soojin
